newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 19.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Inflows of foreign investment in India totalled $4.0 billion in April to December last year, up sharply from $2.6 billion for the same period in 1995, Reserve Bank of India governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said on Tuesday.
He told a conference on infrastructure that foreign
institutional investment (FII) in the eight months more than doubled to $2.3 billion, compared with $1.1 billion in the year-ago period.
Foreign direct investment (FDI) rose to $1.7 billion in the eight months, up from $1.5 billion in the same period of 1995.
** Indian Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Tuesday annual gross domestic product growth could be raised above eight percent if the country's creaking infrastructure is improved.
India's GDP growth was currently running around seven
percent annually, Chidamabaram told a gathering of business people and bankers attending a conference on infrastructure development in the western state of Maharashtra.
"If we can improve infrastructure we can take this up to
over eight percent," he told the "Advantage Maharashtra" conference in Bombay by video link from New Delhi.
But the country needs to invest around $130 billion over
the next five to seven years in its infrastructure sector.

** The Economic Times said on Wednesday, Reliance Industries was holding a letter of comfort from its investment bankers for raising another $500 million of debt for maturities between 10 and 30 years from international investors.
The company has already raised $914 million through the
debt route in the last one-and-a-half years, the paper says.
MARKETS:

** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.89/90 against the dollar on Wednesday and was expected to be range-bound during the day, dealers said. The day's range is seen at 35.88/92 rupees to a dollar, they said.

** Massive sell orders in a day marked by speculative trends saw Indian stocks close sharply lower on Tuesday. The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange shed 50.06 points, or 1.4 percent, to end at 3,530.23
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index slumped 19.35 points, or 1.90 percent, to 1,00.75.
** The Delhi share index lost 1.1 percent to 747.62.
** The Calcutta share index was down 0.77 percent to 453.19.
** The Madras share index slipped 0.65 percent to 3,383.88.
